messages:
Liam (ACME): Hi team — onboarding check. We just started smoke tests against the Redwood SDK and seeing a mix of 401s and 429s during our ramp. Guessing auth or rate limits. Any quick ideas?
Jordan (CS): Thanks for reporting, Liam. Can you paste the exact error body for the 401 and the header x-request-id if present?
Liam (ACME): 401 body: "{\"error\":\"invalid_token\",\"message\":\"token expired or invalid\"}". I grabbed one header: x-request-id: 2f7a3b1c. For 429s response: "rate limit exceeded" with Retry-After: 10.
Olivia (DevEx): Quick checklist: 1) confirm you're sending Authorization: Bearer <key>, 2) check key scopes/expiry in the portal, 3) ensure your CI isn't accidentally rotating keys mid-test.
Maya (Platform Eng): Also check that your load test isn't reusing the same ephemeral key across many parallel clients — that can trigger per-key rate windows. Do you have client_id per instance?
Liam (ACME): We use a single service key in a single process that spawns 50 worker threads to simulate concurrency.
Jordan (CS): That's likely the 429 cause. For the 401s, can you try a curl against the token introspect endpoint? Example: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/status` and paste full response.
Liam (ACME): Ran that: HTTP/1.1 200 OK; body has account_id: acme-123 and scopes: ["inference:read","inference:write"]. So token seems valid.
Maya (Platform Eng): Ok token OK. 401s may be intermittent due to clock skew or a proxy mutating headers. Does your infra run through a corporate proxy or API gateway?
Liam (ACME): Yes we have an internal sidecar that injects headers. Could it be stripping Authorization sometimes?
Olivia (DevEx): Very possible. Add logging at the sidecar egress to confirm the Authorization header is present on outbound requests. Logging snippet: ```js
// node fetch wrapper
const res = await fetch(url, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`}});
console.log('outbound headers', Object.fromEntries(res.request?.headers || []));
```
Jordan (CS): For the 429s during ramp: two mitigations — 1) client-side exponential backoff + jitter, 2) request us to temporarily increase your burst quota while you ramp. Which do you prefer?
Liam (ACME): We'll implement backoff but for the immediate demo this afternoon an elevated burst window would help.
Jordan (CS): Copy that. @maya can you check if we can provision a temporary burst bump for acme-123?
Maya (Platform Eng): I can, but need the account_id and the time window. Liam, how long and what qps are you planning?
Liam (ACME): Planning a 5-minute demo at ~120 qps sustained with spikes to 200 qps.
Maya (Platform Eng): Ok sending to infra for a +2x burst for 10 minutes. Onboard-bot, please create a ticket.
onboard-bot: Created ticket RED-4791 for ACME burst request. Assigned to platform-scaling, priority: high.
Jordan (CS): Also set the client retry policy to something like: ```json
{\"max_retries\": 5, \"initial_backoff_ms\": 200, \"max_backoff_ms\": 5000, \"jitter\": true}
``` That will smooth spikes and cut 429s in production.
Liam (ACME): Implemented that in our SDK wrapper. Two follow-ups: how to detect the 401 pattern vs transient network auth failure so we can fail-fast?
Olivia (DevEx): Treat persistent 401s (>=2 straight attempts) as fatal and alert your ops. For transient auth errors accompanied by x-request-id, send the id to CS and we'll trace on our side.
Jordan (CS): I'll watch the ticket and correlate x-request-ids. If you hit a 401 again, include one sample request/response with headers (sanitized) and we'll check token TTL and our edge logs.
Liam (ACME): Great — one last thing: any recommended log fields to capture?
Olivia (DevEx): Capture timestamp, x-request-id, request path, Authorization presence (boolean), response_status, response_body_snippet, and client concurrency at the moment. Example line: `2026-03-15T14:02:03Z id=2f7a3b1c path=/v1/generate auth_present=true status=200 conc=48`
Maya (Platform Eng): Ticket updated: RED-4791 -> platform-scaling has elevated burst for acme-123 from 14:50 to 15:00 UTC. Watch for 429s after 15:02 for cooldown.
Liam (ACME): Demo went well with the burst bump. We still saw a handful of 401s (about 3) during the peak. I attached one sample with x-request-id: 2f7a3b1c and sanitized headers.
Jordan (CS): Thanks — we'll pull the edge trace for 2f7a3b1c and report back. Can you also confirm if those 401s happen from the same client process or across multiple hosts?
Liam (ACME): Looks like same host process.
Olivia (DevEx): That supports the proxy hypothesis. If the sidecar is rate-limiting header size or doing connection pooling it could drop Authorization on retry. Consider binding fewer workers per process or ensuring the header is reapplied on each retry.
Jordan (CS): Follow-up action: Jordan to review edge trace (x-request-id), Maya to review burst metrics + rate-limiter logs, Olivia to share a short checklist for customer-side logs. Liam to paste any fresh 401 samples in RED-4791.
Liam (ACME): Thanks all — will post updates in the ticket. :thumbsup:
Jordan (CS): Thanks — marking this thread resolved for now. Reopen if you see more 401s after sidecar logging. :eyes:
